about.title: Oakley Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Oakley's mix of agricultural land, growing residential development, and commercial corridors along Main Street and E Cypress Road means workplace injuries here span everything from delivery-driver collisions to warehouse falls and equipment accidents. In California, workers' compensation is generally the only path against your employer, no matter who caused the accident — but if a subcontractor, property owner, equipment manufacturer, or another driver contributed to your injury, you may also have a separate third-party claim worth pursuing. That second track can matter, since workers' comp alone often doesn't cover full damages. LawProactive doesn't practice law or handle your claim directly; we simply connect injured workers in Oakley with an independent attorney who can review both the workers' comp side and any third-party angle, at no upfront cost. If you were injured while working anywhere in Contra Costa County, it's worth having someone look at the whole picture before you sign anything or accept a settlement.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Your Oakley Workplace Injury

items.title: Third-Party Claims Aren't Automatic
items.desc: Workers' comp usually bars claims against your employer, but a negligent subcontractor, equipment maker, or other driver can still be pursued separately — an attorney can spot that opportunity.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Move Fast
items.desc: California requires you to report a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, and missing that window can complicate your case regardless of how serious the injury is.

items.title: Retaliation Protections Exist
items.desc: It's illegal for an employer to punish you for reporting an injury or filing a claim, and an attorney can help you understand your rights if that happens.

items.question: Can I still file a claim if my employer says the accident was my fault?
items.answer: Yes — California workers' compensation generally doesn't require proving fault, since it's a no-fault system for workplace injuries. Fault matters more if there's a separate third-party claim, such as against a subcontractor or equipment supplier.

items.question: What if my injury happened while driving for work near Empire Avenue or Laurel Road?
items.answer: If another driver caused the collision while you were working, you may have both a workers' comp claim and a separate injury claim against that driver. An attorney can help sort out how those two claims interact.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a third-party injury claim in California?
items.answer: Third-party claims — separate from workers' comp — generally carry a two-year deadline from the date of injury under California law. It's best to have your situation reviewed well before that window closes.
